text: At 82 minutes, Ironvale Athletic changed their strategy to press higher and play more direct passes to chase the game. This helped them go from no shots or chances created to 5 shots and a total chance quality (xG) of 0.65 – meaning their shots had about a 65% chance of leading to a goal. They also took control of most of the opponent’s half, flipping field advantage from 6% to 60%. Meanwhile, Redmond Rovers’ chances dropped sharply, showing Ironvale’s new approach really shook things up late in the match[#1477].

To chase the game, their coach instructed a tactical change to press higher (press increased from 0.22 to 0.4) and play more direct (directness from 0.66 to 0.81), while raising their defensive line slightly (line height from 0.25 to 0.37) [#1477].  
- This tactical shift aimed to transform Ironvale’s style from a defensive, counter-attacking posture into a more aggressive, pressing approach to regain possession higher up the pitch and facilitate quicker attacks into the opponent’s box. The directness increase reflects an intent to exploit vertical passing over build-up, consistent with their overall style but now more urgent.  
- The effect was a dramatic increase in offensive threat: post-change, Ironvale generated 5 shots, 10 box touches, and a strong field tilt of 60% vs. only 5.6% before the change, while their xG rose from 0 to 0.65. At the same time, their pressing loosened a bit defensively (ppda slightly improved from 8.0 to 7.2), indicating a balanced risk in pressing further up [#1477].
